newsitem.title: USA: Two U.S. Democrats back China MFN renewal.
newsitem.headline: Two U.S. Democrats back China MFN renewal.

text.p: Two Democratic lawmakers said Tuesday they will support renewal of Most Favored Nation trade status for China, but predicted this year's debate on the topic will be especially acrimonious.

Sen. Joseph Lieberman of Connecticut, who said his state exports $100 million worth of goods to China each year, said denial of MFN would aid other nations' business with China at the expense of U.S. companies and workers.
Rep. Bob Matsui of California, the senior Democrat on the Ways and Means Trade subcommittee, said that denial of MFN would be equivalent to cutting off diplomatic relations.

"The U.S.-China relationship is probably the most important bilateral relationship the United States will have over the next 25 years," Matsui said. "It is my opinion if we cut off MFN with China it could be the equivalent of cutting off diplomatic relations with China," he added.

Matsui and Lieberman spoke at a news conference with the centrist Democratic Leadership Council and Progressive Policy Institute (PPI), both of which urged Congress to debate relations with China after approval of MFN.
"MFN is simply the wrong arena for China debate. MFN is not foreign aid. It is not a favor to, or special privilege for China," the PPI's Bob Manning said.
